evals.name: add_fkeys_to_sym
evals.prompt: I want to add F1-F12 to my sym_func layer in /home/olion/zmk-config-totem/config/totem.keymap. Right now that layer is all &trans placeholders. Use a numpad-style layout on the LEFT hand: F1-F3 on bottom row (positions LB3 LB2 LB1, which are the three middle keys of the bottom row), F4-F6 on home row middle (LM3 LM2 LM1), F7-F9 on top row (LT3 LT2 LT1). Put F10/F11/F12 somewhere reasonable on the same hand. Leave the right hand of sym_func with &trans. Preserve the existing alignment style in the file. Show me the updated sym_func layer block.
evals.expected_output: Updated totem.keymap with F1-F12 placed on the left hand of sym_func layer following numpad style. Right hand remains &trans. Original file structure and alignment preserved.
expectations: F7, F8, F9 are placed on top row positions LT3, LT2, LT1 (positions 1, 2, 3 in declaration order)
F4, F5, F6 are placed on home row middle positions LM3, LM2, LM1
F1, F2, F3 are placed on bottom row middle positions LB3, LB2, LB1
F10, F11, F12 are placed somewhere on the left hand of the sym_func layer
Right hand of sym_func layer remains &trans (or &none in obvious not-yet-mapped positions)
The output preserves the rough column alignment of the existing file
The base, nav_num, and device layers are NOT modified
The behaviors block, includes, and combos.dtsi are NOT modified

evals.name: smart_shift_thumb
evals.prompt: I want a smart-shift behavior on my right thumb (currently &repeat in totem.keymap). New behavior: tap once = sticky-shift (one-shot shift for the next key), tap twice = caps-word (auto-shift letters until I hit a non-letter), hold = regular shift held down. Use mod-morph for the double-tap detection (NOT tap-dance, which would add latency to the single-tap path). Use zmk-helpers macros — this repo includes helper.h. Show me the new behavior definition (where to add it) and the updated base layer binding. Explain briefly why mod-morph beats tap-dance here.
evals.expected_output: A new hold-tap + mod-morph behavior pair (e.g., 'smart_shift' wrapping a tap into a mod-morph that escalates to caps-word when shift is already held). Replacement of the right-thumb &repeat with the new behavior. Brief explanation of the no-delay trick.
expectations: Defines a new hold-tap behavior (using ZMK_HOLD_TAP or raw devicetree) whose hold action is shift (LSHFT or RSHFT) and tap action chains into a mod-morph
Defines a mod-morph whose default binding is &sk LSHFT (sticky shift) and whose shifted binding is &caps_word
The mod-morph's mods include MOD_LSFT (the morph triggers when shift is already held — this is the 'double tap' detection trick)
Updates the base layer binding to replace the right-thumb &repeat with the new behavior
Explains that mod-morph avoids the tap-dance single-tap latency by using sticky-shift as a transient flag
Uses zmk-helpers macro syntax (ZMK_HOLD_TAP, ZMK_MOD_MORPH) rather than raw devicetree since the repo uses helper.h
Does not introduce new west.yml module dependencies (this can all be done with stock ZMK + zmk-helpers)

evals.name: fix_build_errors
evals.prompt:
My GitHub Actions ZMK build is failing for my totem config. Here's the relevant error output:

```
error: totem.keymap.pre.tmp:147.28-147.34:
  Reference to non-existent node or label "hml_sk"

keymap.dts.pre.tmp:163: error: 'BCKSPC' undeclared (first use in this function)

error: keymap.dts.pre.tmp:189.5: 'flavour' is not in the enumeration: ('tap-preferred', 'hold-preferred', 'balanced', 'tap-unless-interrupted')
```

Help me diagnose each error and tell me exactly how to fix each one. For each error: explain what it means in plain language, what likely caused it, and the specific fix.
evals.expected_output: Three diagnostics, each with: explanation of the error meaning, the likely cause, and the specific fix. The user should be able to apply each fix without further research.
expectations: Error 1 (hml_sk reference) is correctly diagnosed as a missing or misspelled behavior definition — the user used &hml_sk in a binding but didn't define hml_sk: ... anywhere, or included the file defining it AFTER its use
Error 1 fix suggests either defining the behavior or correcting the spelling (e.g., to &hml)
Error 2 (BCKSPC undeclared) is correctly diagnosed as a keycode typo — BCKSPC is not a valid ZMK keycode
Error 2 fix specifies the correct spelling: BSPC (or BACKSPACE)
Error 3 (flavour) is correctly diagnosed as British vs American spelling — ZMK uses 'flavor', not 'flavour'
Error 3 fix specifies changing flavour to flavor
Explanations are clear enough that a non-expert can apply the fix
Does not invent additional errors that weren't in the output
